body:
This is probably due to the safe save system which creates a temporary file for writing and then moves that file to replace the original, replacing the permissions

The solution here is probably to check the permissions and error instead, but that would require a bit more integration unless it's just a plain text error (we'd otherwise have to integrate this into the editor interface somehow for opening read-only files), I'd say in general the assumption of the editor should be that it just has permission to the entire project

Marking this as Windows specific because it's implemented for windows specifically, similar issues might exist for Linux and other platforms I can't test, but the specific issue is in the Windows code, though the editor interface for it can be potentially improved separately

> [...] in general the assumption of the editor should be that it just has permission to the entire project

Formally working under that assumption would essentially make locking version control with systems such as P4 or SVN a non-starter, which would be disappointing seeing as most non-programmers would _really_ benefit from not having to know what a merge conflict is.

>  [...] the specific issue is in the Windows code [...]

Could you cite what code that would be? Because the problem I'm reporting is one I'm actively experiencing on Linux. Last I checked on Windows, it would refuse to open any scenes if it didn't have read permission (keep in mind, this was quite a while ago, I have no Windows installation to test with), and that's bad. _But_ the problem I have on Linux, silently changing permissions, is in my opinion worse since that _breaks the promise that a locking version control system makes_ about its locks.

> Formally working under that assumption would essentially make locking version control with systems such as P4 or SVN a non-starter, which would be disappointing seeing as most non-programmers would really benefit from not having to know what a merge conflict is.

What I mean is that the editor is built around that logic, not that it's necessarily correct, but I'd say that the editor shouldn't treat it special for the interface but instead handle the errors correctly 

> Could you cite what code that would be? Because the problem I'm reporting is one I'm actively experiencing on Linux. 

My bad I missed this was reported on Linux! Then it's a different but related issue, it's probably the same issue but a different platform, will adjust! Thank you for clarifying

I haven't done all that much reading of Godot's source code, and I'll admit I'm not *too* familiar with C-style file access, but it seems to me that an error would only be encountered if `is_backup_save_enabled()` returns false. If backup save is enabled, it seems to me like the flow would be opening a temporary file, copying the mode and permission bits from the original to the new one, use it, close it, rename it to the original's name.

I tried writing a program that did that and it ended up *almost* behaving like Godot. It changed the read-only file's contents, but *it kept the permissions*. So I ended up with an altered file with read-only permissions still attached.

I wonder if the "fallback permissions" here might somehow be to blame:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1ea6b0ccff9962ec93c4008e66b4f83cb57b9023/drivers/unix/file_access_unix.cpp#L156-L161

That wouldn't make much sense since it would seemingly only be used if `stat` has an error, and `stat` shouldn't error when used on a read-only file... But when I get home I'll try to see if `strace` can give me any clues there.

Try running with the backup save feature disabled, if it still changes the permissions that probably points to a different issue, so it could either be due to the `stat` erroring (I'd add an error print to the `else` branch for example) and check the `rename` method it might just ignore stat data

I can't currently test any of this on Linux unfortunately, I will read up some on the posix methods though later today

Took me a while, I ended up forgetting, sorry about that. I've now tried switching off the backup save option. At first I thought it had no effect, but after restarting Godot it now correctly gives an error on saving. So as far as I'm concerned that confirms that the problem comes from backup saves being new files renamed to the old name. It does *not* explain why the newly created file gets its write bit set, since my test program that did pretty much the same thing had no such behavior.

The answer to the last point probably doesn't matter much though, it would likely be sufficient to check the original's permissions before attempting to save the temporary version, and error out if we're not supposed to be able to write to it. Then it just becomes a matter of polishing the error, and perhaps adding a little warning lock icon on the tab.

This is still happening in 4.6. And applies to all files not just scenes. Reproduced this with any binary file. What might be also worth mentioning is that the exact behaviour seems to have shifted a bit. What I noticed is that: 

- v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6] and v4.5.stable.official [876b29033] seem to change the permissions of the file.
- v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e] seems to leave the file permissions as is, but still overwrites it.

It might be good to say is that this is a serious problem for working in teams bigger than a few people. File locking is central to Perforce and using Git LFS locking is a practically a requirement for using Git. Having the engine just ignore the file permissions means a project won't be able to scale.

If we could get anything, anything at all - popup, toaster message, console error, saying that a file cannot be saved, that would be much better, than a file being quietly overwritten.

Created a PR to fix this. The root (unintuitive?) piece is that POSIX only checks the destination _folder_ permissions for rename; it does not check the _file_ permissions. This is different than Windows whose rename API (Godot uses `ReplaceFileW`) does check for target path writability.

POSIX reference if you want to be cool at parties: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/rename.html

> Write access permission is required for the directory containing old and the directory containing new.
